--- title: "[Outcome]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A reusable description of a survival response: column names plus an event encoding. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L69-L620){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Outcome( kind, columns, event_value=None, censor_value=None, states=None, state_values=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} An `Outcome` says which columns hold the response and how to read the event, but holds no data. Pass it to any estimator's `fit()` together with `data=`. The estimator reads every column it needs from that one frame, drops rows with missing values once (as R's `na.omit` does), and fits. Because the description is made of column names and values rather than DataFrame expressions, the same `Outcome` works on any backend: pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, or a lazy frame. Build one with the class methods, which mirror the `Surv` constructors (`right`, `left`, `counting`, `interval`, `multistate`), or parse an R-style formula response with `Outcome.from_formula()`. Call `bind()` to turn it into a `Surv` for a particular frame. ::: ## Parameter Attributes {.doc-parameter-attributes} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [kind]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[tuple[str, str | Duration], ...]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : [event_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : [censor_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : [states]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : [state_values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[Any, ...] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Describe the `lung` endpoint once, where a `status` of `2` means the patient died: ::: {#f759109a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Name the columns and the event encoding, with no data attached yet death = gw.Outcome.right(time="time", event="status", event_value=2) death ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Outcome.right(time='time', event='status', event_value=2) ``` ::: ::: Pass the description to an estimator along with the frame. Column names work for covariates and for `by=` too: ::: {#43b1f024 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} lung = gw.load_dataset("lung") # Fit a Cox model and a stratified Kaplan-Meier curve from the same description cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(death, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=lung) km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, by="sex", data=lung) cox ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` CoxPH (Cox proportional hazards model, ties='efron') coef exp(coef) se(coef) z p age 0.01705 1.017 0.009223 1.848 0.06459 sex -0.5132 0.5986 0.1675 -3.065 0.002178 n = 228, events = 165 Likelihood ratio test = 14.12 on 2 df, p = 0.0008574 ``` ::: ::: The same response can be written as a formula, which is parsed into an `Outcome`: ::: {#4d0e36d3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} gw.Outcome.from_formula(formula="Surv(time, status == 2)") == death ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
column_names The distinct column names the response reads, in argument order.
### [column_names]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The distinct column names the response reads, in argument order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [column_names]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
bind() Build a `Surv` response from the columns of `data`.
counting() Describe a counting-process `(start, stop]` response.
first_event() Describe a competing-risks response built from several endpoint column pairs.
from_formula() Parse an R-style formula response such as `"Surv(time, status == 2)"`.
interval() Describe an interval-censored response.
left() Describe a left-censored response.
multistate() Describe a multi-state or competing-risks response.
right() Describe a right-censored response.
### [bind()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Build a `Surv` response from the columns of `data`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L559-L620){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python bind(data) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `bind()` is strict: missing values in the response columns raise an error, as they do in the `Surv` constructors. To drop incomplete rows automatically, pass the `Outcome` to an estimator's `fit()` with `data=` instead, where the response and covariates are filtered together. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) or a mapping of column names to values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Surv]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The response for this frame. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#21118803 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung") gw.Outcome.right(time="time", event="status", event_value=2).bind(lung) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Surv(type=right, n=228, events=165) ``` ::: ::: ### [counting()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Describe a counting-process `(start, stop]` response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L217-L264){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python counting( start, stop, event=None, *, weights=None, event_value=None, censor_value=None ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [start]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding entry times, or a `duration()`. [stop]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding exit times, or a `duration()` computed from two date columns. [event]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding the event indicator. If `None`, every row is an event. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding case weights (optional). [event_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value (or list of values) in `event` that marks an event. See `Surv.counting()`. [censor_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value (or list of values) in `event` that marks censoring. Pass this or `event_value`, not both. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Outcome]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data-free description of the response. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#6e3217b8 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Outcome.counting(start="tstart", stop="tstop", event="event") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` Outcome.counting(start='tstart', stop='tstop', event='event') ``` ::: ::: ### [first_event()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Describe a competing-risks response built from several endpoint column pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L361-L430){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python first_event(endpoints, *, censor_at=None, start=None, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each endpoint has its own time and event column. For each row, the earliest observed event wins, ties go to the endpoint listed first, and rows with no observed event are censored at the latest endpoint time (or at `censor_at`). See `Surv.first_event()`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [endpoints]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Mapping[str, Sequence[Any]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A mapping of state label to `(time, event)` or `(time, event, event_value)` column names, in priority order for ties. [censor_at]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding the censoring time for rows with no observed event (optional). [start]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding entry times, for late entry (optional). [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding case weights (optional). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Outcome]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data-free description of the response. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#14fd54f9 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # PCM and death are recorded in separate column pairs in mgus2 cr = gw.Outcome.first_event( endpoints={"pcm": ("ptime", "pstat"), "death": ("futime", "death")} ) gw.AalenJohansen().fit(cr, data=gw.load_dataset("mgus2")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` AalenJohansen (Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence) states: pcm, death n = 1384 final CIF pcm 0.1613 death 0.8387 ``` ::: ::: ### [from_formula()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Parse an R-style formula response such as `"Surv(time, status == 2)"`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L432-L478){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python from_formula(formula) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The response is written as a call to `Surv()` with column names and literal values. The forms follow R's `survival::Surv()`: - `Surv(time)`: every row is an event - `Surv(time, event)`: `event` is boolean or `0`/`1` - `Surv(time, status == 2)` or `Surv(time, status != 0)`: declare the event value, or the censoring value - `Surv(time, status in (1, 2))`: several event values (R's `%in% c(1, 2)` is accepted too) - `Surv(start, stop, event)`: the counting-process form - `Surv(time, event, type="left")` and `Surv(lower, upper, type="interval2")` - `Surv(time, cause, states={"pcm": 1, "death": 2})`: a multi-state response Keyword arguments `event_value=`, `censor_value=`, `weights=`, and `states=` may also be given inside the call. Column names that are not valid Python identifiers can be quoted with backticks. Dotted R names such as `ph.ecog` work without quoting. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The response, optionally followed by `~ 1`. To include covariates, pass the full formula to an estimator's `fit()` instead. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Outcome]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data-free description of the response. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#7c3b8145 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Outcome.from_formula(formula="Surv(time, status == 2)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` Outcome.right(time='time', event='status', event_value=2) ``` ::: ::: ### [interval()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Describe an interval-censored response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L266-L294){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python interval(lower, upper, *, weights=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [lower]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding interval lower bounds. [upper]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding interval upper bounds (`inf` for right-censored rows). [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding case weights (optional). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Outcome]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data-free description of the response. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#3e49e830 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Outcome.interval(lower="left", upper="right") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` Outcome.interval(lower='left', upper='right') ``` ::: ::: ### [left()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Describe a left-censored response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L171-L215){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python left(time, event=None, *, weights=None, event_value=None, censor_value=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding observation times, or a `duration()`. [event]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding the event indicator. If `None`, every row is an event. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding case weights (optional). [event_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value (or list of values) in `event` that marks an event. See `Surv.left()`. [censor_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value (or list of values) in `event` that marks an event-free row. Pass this or `event_value`, not both. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Outcome]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data-free description of the response. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#fe583c51 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Outcome.left(time="time", event="detected", event_value="yes") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ``` Outcome.left(time='time', event='detected', event_value='yes') ``` ::: ::: ### [multistate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Describe a multi-state or competing-risks response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L296-L359){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python multistate(time, event, states, *, start=None, weights=None, censor_value=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding event or censoring times, or a `duration()`. [event]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding the outcome. [states]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[str] | Mapping[str, Any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A mapping of state label to the `event` value (or values) marking it, such as `{"pcm": 1, "death": 2}`, or a sequence of labels when `event` already holds codes `0, 1, 2, ...`. See `Surv.multistate()`. [start]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding entry times, for late entry (optional). [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding case weights (optional). [censor_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value (or list of values) in `event` that marks censoring when `states` is a mapping. The default is `0`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Outcome]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data-free description of the response. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#1097a326 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Outcome.multistate(time="etime", event="cause", states={"pcm": 1, "death": 2}) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ``` Outcome.multistate(time='etime', event='cause', states={'pcm': 1, 'death': 2}) ``` ::: ::: ### [right()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Describe a right-censored response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_outcome.py#L124-L169){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python right(time, event=None, *, weights=None, event_value=None, censor_value=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding exit times, or a `duration()` computed from two date columns. [event]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding the event indicator. If `None`, every row is an event. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column holding case weights (optional). [event_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value (or list of values) in `event` that marks an event. Every other row is censored. See `Surv.right()`. [censor_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value (or list of values) in `event` that marks censoring. Every other row is an event. Pass this or `event_value`, not both. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Outcome]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A data-free description of the response. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#76de72da .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Outcome.right(time="time", event="status", event_value=2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ``` Outcome.right(time='time', event='status', event_value=2) ``` ::: :::
